Branch of the LORD
branch of the lord
noun
Hebrew Tsemach Yahweh (H6780) — "Branch of Yahweh"; a Messianic title appearing principally in Isa 4:2; Jer 23:5; 33:15; Zech 3:8; 6:12 — the promised Davidic king who would be both shoot from a stump and the great priest-king ruling forever.

📖 Biblical Definition

Branch of the LORD is one of the great Messianic titles of the OT, gathering up the prophetic expectation of a Davidic descendant who would unite kingly and priestly office and rule forever. The title appears at five major prophetic locations, each adding a facet: (1) ISAIAH 4:2 — "In that day shall the branch of the LORD be beautiful and glorious" (the Branch as the glory revealed in the day of the LORD); (2) ISAIAH 11:1 — though the word is netser (a related term), "there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots" (the Branch as shoot from the cut-down Davidic line); (3) JEREMIAH 23:5 — "I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth" (the Branch as righteous reigning king); (4) ZECHARIAH 3:8 — "behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH" (the Branch as God's appointed servant); (5) ZECHARIAH 6:12-13 — "Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH... he shall build the temple of the LORD; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be A PRIEST upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both" (the Branch as priest-king uniting both offices that the OT had carefully kept separate, since Aaron's line and David's line were distinct). Christ fulfills all five: He is the glory revealed (Isa 4:2 / John 1:14), the shoot from Jesse's stump after the Davidic line had been cut down by the exile (Isa 11:1 / Matt 1), the righteous reigning king (Jer 23:5 / Rev 19), the Servant (Zech 3:8 / Phil 2:6-11), and the priest-king after the order of Melchizedek (Zech 6:12-13 / Heb 7). The Branch grows quietly from the stump no one expected to sprout.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A Messianic title gathering five prophetic locations (Isa 4:2; Isa 11:1; Jer 23:5; Zech 3:8; Zech 6:12); the Davidic shoot uniting kingly and priestly offices.

BRANCH OF THE LORD, noun. A Messianic title appearing at five major prophetic locations: Isa 4:2; Isa 11:1 (related word netser); Jer 23:5; Zech 3:8; Zech 6:12-13. Hebrew Tsemach Yahweh.

The Branch is the promised Davidic descendant — shoot from a stump, righteous reigning king, God's Servant, and (uniquely) priest-king uniting offices that the OT had kept separate. All five fulfilled in Christ.

📖 Key Scripture

Zechariah 6:12-13 — "Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the LORD: Even he shall build the temple of the LORD; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both."

Jeremiah 23:5 — "Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth."

Isaiah 4:2 — "In that day shall the branch of the LORD be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the earth shall be excellent and comely for them that are escaped of Israel."

Isaiah 11:1 — "And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Branch of the LORD is corrupted when the priest-king typology of Zechariah 6:12-13 is severed from Christ's high-priestly work (Hebrews 7), or when each individual Branch passage is read in isolation rather than as a unified canonical chorus.

expand to see more

Priest-king severance. Zechariah 6:12-13 uniquely promises a Branch who would be BOTH king AND priest — "he shall be a priest upon his throne." The OT had kept these offices strictly separated: Aaron's line was priestly; David's line was royal; King Uzziah was struck with leprosy for trying to combine them (2 Chr 26:16-21). The Branch unites what the OT had carefully kept apart. Hebrews 7 expounds this: Christ as priest after the order of Melchizedek (not Aaron) holds both offices forever, fulfilling Zechariah 6:12-13 exactly. To strip this typology is to lose the key explanation of why Christ's priesthood is superior to Aaron's.

Isolated-passage reading. Modern preaching sometimes treats each Branch passage in isolation — Isaiah's Branch is one thing, Jeremiah's another, Zechariah's another. But the canonical pattern is unified: five passages, all using the same root tsemach (or related netser), all describing the same coming Messianic figure with complementary facets. The Branch is glory revealed (Isa 4:2), shoot from cut-down stump (Isa 11:1), righteous king (Jer 23:5), Servant (Zech 3:8), priest-king (Zech 6:12-13). To read them as five separate prophecies of five different things is to miss the Spirit's unified canonical work.

Hebrew Tsemach Yahweh (H6780) — Branch of Yahweh; the Messianic shoot promised across five major prophetic locations.

Hebrew tsemach (H6780) — branch, shoot, sprout; the Messianic title used by Isaiah, Jeremiah, and Zechariah

Related: Hebrew netser (Isa 11:1) — shoot, branch — different word but same Messianic concept; root of "Nazareth" / "Nazarene"

Five major Branch passages: Isa 4:2; Isa 11:1; Jer 23:5; Zech 3:8; Zech 6:12-13 — each adds a facet of the same coming Messiah

Unites kingly and priestly offices the OT had kept strictly separate — fulfilled in Christ as priest after Melchizedek (Heb 7)

Usage

"Behold the man whose name is the Branch — Zechariah's word for the Messiah who would be both king AND priest."

"The Branch grows from the cut-down stump no one expected to sprout — Israel's Davidic line, dead in exile, sprouted in Bethlehem."

"Christ fulfills all five Branch passages: glory revealed, shoot from Jesse, righteous king, Servant, priest-king after Melchizedek."
